title: Neutral inline model — fragment to merge into neutral-interchange.schema.json
description: Feature 016. Replaces the plain-string text positions of $defs.content_blocks with marked spans, and adds the ordered_list block kind. Merge target: specs/001-jira-reconcile-engine/contracts/neutral-interchange.schema.json (edited in place — it is the living contract; see research.md section 5). NO ADF node or mark names appear here: neutral bold/italic/monospace/strikethrough map to ADF strong/em/code/strike in the sink, and only in the sink.

kind.description: Neutral formatting vocabulary. Deliberately lexically distinct from ADF's strong/em/code/strike (Constitution VIII).

href.description: Absolute http(s) target. Required iff kind is 'link'. The pattern is the schema-level backstop for FR-006: a non-http target can never reach Jira as a live link, because a validation failure blocks every downstream write.

text.description: Literal characters a reader sees. Never carries the syntax of a converted construct (FR-002).

marks.description: Always present, [] when unmarked, sorted alphabetically by kind. Always-emitted and always-sorted so the two ports cannot differ by an omitted key or by source nesting order (FR-015).

inline.description: A sequence of marked runs. Empty array represents empty text. Invariant not expressible in JSON Schema and enforced by the tokenizer instead (contract D1): no two consecutive spans carry equal marks.

content_blocks.description: A neutral, Jira-agnostic block tree. The sink renders it to ADF. NO ADF node names appear here.

type.description: Neutral block kinds. 'ordered_list' is new in feature 016 (FR-008). 'panel_ref' marks where the sink should place a panel; the engine does not know what a Jira panel is.

items.description: List items. Each item is an inline sequence — was an array of plain strings before feature 016.

text.description: Code block body ONLY. Deliberately plain: FR-007 forbids interpreting markup inside code, and keeping this position a string makes that a property of the schema rather than a rule the tokenizer must remember.

ref.description: For panel_ref: a logical section name, e.g. 'acceptance_criteria' or 'design'.

acceptance_criterion_clause.description: Feature 016: acceptance_criteria given/when/then entries become inline sequences instead of plain strings. This replaces the crude global asterisk strip at engine/parse.sh:199, which was the partial workaround for this defect.

design_item_value.description: Feature 016: design[].value becomes an inline sequence when kind is 'guidance', and stays a plain string URL when kind is 'figma_link' (a URL is not prose).
